tools.name: list_schemas
tools.description: List schemas

tools.name: get_op_schema
tools.description: Get an edit operation schema. The example is a single op object, ready to drop into an edit request's `ops` array, not a whole request body.

op.description: Op name: set_properties, update_block, replace_subtree, insert_blocks, move_block, delete_block, replace_text, set_cell, update_view, insert_view, move_view, delete_view, add_items, remove_items

tools.name: get_schema
tools.description: Get a schema

kind.description: Schema kind, as listed by list_schemas

tools.name: search_global
tools.description: Search objects across spaces. Type keys and option names resolve per space; unresolved spaces produce warnings. Searches loaded spaces using query as full text over names and indexed content. total is a lower bound when clipped; use has_more to request further pages. Warnings report loading or unavailable stores. Each row carries space_id.

fields.description: property keys to include per row, as an array such as ["status","due_date"]; the list reads take the same keys as one comma-separated string

filter.description: compact filter string (grammar on kind filters), an alternative to the structured filters array; a body sends at most one of the two

filters.description: structured filter nodes (schema kind filters), an alternative to the compact filter string; a body sends at most one of the two

ids.description: How each row's space_id is spelled: compact (default) is the short space reference; full is the whole <cid>.<replicationKey> id, and the spelling to store outside this API

query.description: full-text query over object names and indexed content

type.description: a type key: only objects of this type

value.description: leaf value. A select or multi_select takes option names, never ids. A date takes unix seconds; where the filter is stored (a query's views, update_view) it also takes a date string such as 2026-08-01 or 2026-08-01T09:00:00Z, converted on write, while search takes a date string only in the compact filter string

tools.name: list_spaces
tools.description: List spaces. Returns only live spaces accessible to this API key. A space that is deleted, left, or still joining does not appear. has_not_granted_spaces is true when other live user spaces are excluded by the key's grant; if a requested space is missing, ask the user to grant access. This flag is independent of pagination: total and has_more describe only accessible spaces.

ids.description: compact (default) is the short space reference; full is the whole <cid>.<replicationKey> id, and the spelling to store outside this API

tools.name: create_space
tools.description: Create a space. A retry the server already handled makes a second space unless it carries the same idempotency key. A dry run validates the body and stops there; creating a space cannot be simulated.

ids.description: compact (default) is the short space reference; full is the whole <cid>.<replicationKey> id of the new space, and the spelling to store outside this API

tools.name: get_space
tools.description: Get a space. Only live spaces are served. A space that is deleted, left, or still joining is a 404.

ids.description: compact (default) is the short space reference; full is the whole <cid>.<replicationKey> id, and the spelling to store outside this API

tools.name: update_space
tools.description: Update a space. At least one of the two fields must be present; a field left out keeps its current value. The space icon and the default object type are not writable through this API.

ids.description: compact (default) is the short space reference; full is the whole <cid>.<replicationKey> id, and the spelling to store outside this API

tools.name: list_chats
tools.description: List chats. Every row carries `unread_messages` and `unread_mentions`, read from the chat state without opening the chat. `include=discussions` adds the space's object discussions: a discussion row's id is the discussion's own id (usable on every chat route) and `parent_id` is the object it belongs to. `unread` keeps only rows with unread messages or unread mentions, and `total` then counts the kept rows.

include.description: discussions adds object discussions to the list; omitted lists chats only

unread.description: messages keeps rows with unread messages; mentions keeps rows with unread mentions

tools.name: create_chat
tools.description: Create a chat. Messages are not blocks. Add them through the messages route; a document edit cannot reach them.

tools.name: get_chat_messages
tools.description: List chat messages. `after` alone walks forward, oldest first, continuing from `next_after`. Every other query is anchored at the newest end and walks backward from `next_before`. Both bounds are exclusive; messages are always ascending. `message_count` is the number of messages the chat holds now; `lifetime_message_count` counts every message ever posted. `offset` is refused.

after.description: Return messages after this order id (exclusive)

before.description: Return messages before this order id (exclusive)

reactions.description: counts (default) returns the emoji counts; full adds the participant ids behind each count

tools.name: add_chat_message
tools.description: Send a chat message. The text is Markdown, formatted as described under Write chat messages. The cap is 8000 UTF-16 code units, where one emoji can cost two or more. Attachments are object ids, at most 32, and each one's kind is taken from the target's layout. In a discussion the text is stored as blocks.

tools.name: edit_chat_message
tools.description: Update chat message text. Every mark is re-derived from the text you send, so a mark the old text carried and the new text does not spell out is lost; in a discussion the text replaces the message's blocks the same way, and dropped quotes or links are named in `warnings`. Attachments and the reply target survive; the style does in a space chat. Editing another member's message is a 403.

text.description: The new text, required so an omitted member cannot clear the message by accident; an empty string clears it on purpose.

tools.name: delete_chat_message
tools.description: Delete a chat message. An attachment whose only reference was this message is erased for good afterwards, not moved to Bin. The response names those ids in `warnings`, and a dry run reports the same list without deleting anything. A message that does not exist is a 404 on the dry run too.

dry_run.description: Report what would be deleted, attachments included, without committing

tools.name: toggle_chat_reaction
tools.description: Toggle a chat reaction. `added` says which way the toggle went. A dry run predicts it, but when there is no account identity to predict with it omits the field and says so in `warnings`.

dry_run.description: Report the would-be outcome without committing

idempotency_key.description: retry key: if this call fails or times out, send it again with the same value so it is not applied twice; one is made for you when omitted

tools.name: read_chat
tools.description: Mark chat activity as read. `up_to` is inclusive; it and `last_state_id` come from one messages read: the newest order and the state's id. An empty value would silently mark nothing, so both are required. Later messages stay unread. The reactions scope takes neither field. The receipt carries the chat's state after the move when it could be read back.

tools.name: publish_chat_status
tools.description: Publish chat status. Publishes encrypted ephemeral JSON on status/<chat_id>. Empty text is omitted so clients can show localized typing. data accepts any JSON value. The encoded payload is limited to 65,508 bytes. Status is not stored or replayed; receivers expire it. Success acknowledges acceptance, not delivery.

data.description: optional arbitrary JSON value: object, array, string, number, boolean or null

text.description: optional display text; empty or omitted is left out of the pubsub payload so receivers can show a localized typing label; JSON escaping and data consume the same byte budget

tools.name: create_collection
tools.description: Create a collection. Item ids are checked against the space; an id that does not resolve there is refused rather than dropped.

tools.name: get_collection_objects
tools.description: List collection objects. A collection's objects are its membership, so without view the whole set comes back in the order the collection stores it and no view filter applies, even when the collection has one view. A view's filters and sorts apply only when view names it.

fields.description: Comma-separated property keys to include per row

view.description: Stored view id (exact or unique suffix). Omitted, no view applies and the whole membership is returned.

tools.name: get_collection_views
tools.description: List collection views

tools.name: upload_file
tools.description: Upload a file. Send multipart/form-data with a `file` field, or JSON {"url": …}. A source that refuses the fetch, or a URL that cannot be fetched, is a 400 naming /url; only a genuine server fault answers 500. The id that comes back is the one file blocks, image blocks and icon_image values reference.

name.description: names the stored object; omit to keep the name the source gives

tools.name: list_members
tools.description: List members

tools.name: get_member_me
tools.description: Get the current member. The identity is taken from the account this API runs against; there is no member id to send.

tools.name: list_objects
tools.description: List objects

fields.description: Comma-separated property keys to include per row

tools.name: create_object
tools.description: Create an object. A select value naming an option the property does not hold is refused unless `create_missing_options=true` is set. An unknown type or property key is rejected either way. The body is a full AnyBlock document or the shortcut {type, name, properties, markdown}; `formatVersion` or `blocks` picks the document form. `template` starts the object from one; absent, the type's `default_template` applies. The document form's schema and a worked example come from get_schema with kind object; the other forms need no lookup.

properties.description: property key → value. A list-shaped key takes an array of option names or object ids; a date takes a date string such as 2026-08-01 or 2026-08-01T09:30:00Z rather than unix seconds

anyOf.description: a full AnyBlock document: formatVersion 2.0, properties, and blocks in preorder. It takes the shortcut's template member too; its schema and a worked example come from get_schema with kind object

inputSchema.description: the shortcut body, or a full AnyBlock document; formatVersion or blocks picks the document form

create_missing_options.description: Create select options for names the property does not hold yet (default false: an unmatched name is refused)

markdown.description: markdown body parsed into blocks server-side, part of the same single create (dry runs validate it too); at most 2048 parsed blocks. Start it at the first section: a leading heading that repeats the name is dropped, and with no name a leading # heading becomes the name

name.description: display name. The object displays it above its body, so a markdown body that repeats it as a heading shows it twice

properties.description: property key → value. A list-shaped key takes an array of option names or object ids; a date takes a date string such as 2026-08-01 or 2026-08-01T09:30:00Z rather than unix seconds

template.description: id of the template this object starts from. Leave it out: the type's default_template applies when it has one, and nothing is applied when it does not. Reading the type first is not needed. The result names the template that was applied, how many blocks it added, and whether the body is those blocks followed by yours. Send "none" to start from nothing

type.description: type key, e.g. page or task

tools.name: get_object
tools.description: Get an object. A `block` subtree comes back flagged as a subtree, and no write path accepts that partial body. `format=md` is read-only; markdown cannot be sent back.

ids.description: compact (default) is the edit shape, where minted block ids relabel to short suffixes; full is the export shape, with full ids everywhere, and the shape to send back. Object references are full and inline in both.

outline.description: Return the outline instead of full blocks: every block's indent/id/type plus its text truncated to 80 runes

tools.name: patch_object
tools.description: Update an object. Edits in place, keeping the id and links; to change the type, use set_type rather than recreating the object. Applies ops in order as one atomic edit. A failed op or invalid result leaves the object unchanged. Text locators must match exactly one block. New block and view IDs are returned by payload position in `created_blocks` and `created_views`, compact by default or full with `ids=full`. Ops and their members, ? marking an optional one: set_properties{add?, remove?, set?, unset?}, set_type{type}, update_block{set, id?, match?}, replace_subtree{id, blocks}, insert_blocks{after?, before?, blocks?, inside?, markdown?, position?}, move_block{id, after?, before?, inside?, position?}, delete_block{id?, match?, recursive?}, replace_text{find, replace, id?, replace_all?}, set_cell{table_id, row, col, value}, update_view{block?, columns?, set?, view?}, insert_view{name, after?, before?, block?, columns?, copy_from?, position?, set?}, move_view{view, after?, before?, block?, position?}, delete_view{view, block?}, add_items{items}, remove_items{items}. get_op_schema with an op's name serves the members' value shapes and a worked example; call it before first using an op whose shapes you do not know.

create_missing_options.description: Create select options for names the property does not hold yet (default false: an unmatched name is refused)

ids.description: ID spelling in created_blocks and created_views

if_match.description: The etag the object must still carry

ops.description: applied in order as one edit, and if any one is refused none is applied. Each op's members, schema and example come from get_op_schema with its op name

tools.name: delete_object
tools.description: Delete an object. Only objects this key created can be deleted. The creator is recorded at creation time and never added later, so objects made in the app, imported, made by another member, or made before this route shipped are refused for good. System objects are a 403 as well. A dry run reports the verdict without the checks that run at archive time, so a deletable verdict can still meet a 403.

tools.name: create_discussion
tools.description: Start an object's discussion. A discussion is the comment thread under an object, and it is a chat: the returned id is the `chat_id` for every chat operation, where `reply_to` makes a threaded reply. An object that already has one answers 200 with the same id and no `created`, so the call is safe to repeat. An object read serves the id as `discussion`. Chats, types, templates and system objects cannot hold one.

dry_run.description: Report whether the object has a discussion without creating one

tools.name: list_properties
tools.description: List properties

tools.name: create_property
tools.description: Create a property. Names are not identities: without an explicit key, a name a visible property already carries is refused. Supply a different available key to create another property with that name; the response carries a warning.

key.description: the key the property is addressed by; derived from the name when omitted. Required to create another property under a display name the space already has

name.description: display name. Names are not identities: without an explicit key, a name a visible property already carries is refused. Supply a different available key to create another property with that name; the response carries a warning

tools.name: update_property
tools.description: Update a property. Only the display name can change. The key is the property's identity, and its format is fixed once it exists.

name.description: the new display name; the key is identity and does not change

tools.name: delete_property
tools.description: Delete a property

tools.description: List property options

tools.name: create_query
tools.description: Create a query. Filter and sort property keys are checked against the type the query runs over; a key that type does not carry is refused.

create_missing_options.description: Create select options for names the property does not hold yet (default false: an unmatched name is refused)

filter.description: compact filter string (grammar on kind filters), an alternative to the structured filters array; a body sends at most one of the two

filters.description: structured filter nodes (schema kind filters), an alternative to the compact filter string; a body sends at most one of the two

views.description: the query's views, each whole: the fields the insert_view op's set takes (except filter: write a view's filters as nodes here), plus its columns. Mutually exclusive with top-level filter/sorts, which build one view named All

group_by.description: property key to group by (kanban/board views)

id.description: output-only on reads; accepted back so a read sort round-trips

value.description: leaf value. A select or multi_select takes option names, never ids. tools.name: get_query_objects
tools.description: List query results. Without view, the query's first stored view applies, so its filters and sorts shape the rows; when the query has several views a warning names the one applied and the others. A view's dynamic placeholders, such as the calling member, are resolved here; one that cannot be resolved becomes a warning rather than a silently empty result.

fields.description: Comma-separated property keys to include per row

view.description: Stored view id (exact or unique suffix). Omitted, the query's first view applies.

tools.name: get_query_views
tools.description: List query views

tools.name: search_space
tools.description: Search objects in a space. `filter` and `filters` are two spellings of the same thing, the compact string and the structured array; sending both is refused. This is a read carried by POST because the query needs a body, so pagination stays in the query string and a `limit` or `offset` in the body is refused.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List templates. `type` narrows the list to the templates of one type. Each row's id is what a create passes in `template`, and `default` marks the one a create of that type starts from on its own.

type.description: Type key: list only the templates that start an object of this type

tools.name: create_template
tools.description: Create a template. `template_for` names the type key this template starts an object of. Body: the template as an AnyBlock document: formatVersion 2.0, kind template, template_for naming the type; its schema and a worked example come from get_schema with kind template.

create_missing_options.description: Create select options for names the property does not hold yet (default false: an unmatched name is refused)

tools.description: Create a type. A `property_definitions` entry naming a property that does not exist creates it alongside the type. The body is either the flat type body or an AnyBlock document with kind "object_type"; `formatVersion`, `kind` or `type_settings` picks the document form. The document form's schema and a worked example come from get_schema with kind type_document; the other forms need no lookup.

layout.description: the layout instances of this type get; basic unless you need another

tools.name: list_widgets
tools.description: List widgets. The sidebar in its order: the space widgets every member sees, then this account's personal ones. `scope` narrows to one of the two. A built-in listing is a target spelled with a leading underscore, such as _favorite or _bin; an object id is served as it is.

scope.description: space or personal; omitted lists both

tools.name: create_widget
tools.description: Create a widget. Adds a widget for an object to the space sidebar (scope space, owner and admins) or to this account's own (scope personal, any member who can write). One widget per target per scope. The layout and limit follow the app's own rules: a layout the target cannot render, or a limit off the app's list, is replaced with the app's fallback and reported in warnings.

after.description: id or target of the sidebar widget to place this one after. At most one of after, before and position; on PATCH, none of the three keeps the position

before.description: id or target of the sidebar widget to place this one before

layout.description: how the widget renders. Omitted on POST, the target's kind picks it: tree for a page, view for a query, collection or type, link for everything else. A layout the target cannot render is replaced with the one it can, with a warning

limit.description: how many entries a listing shows, from the app's own pick-list: 6, 10, 14, 30 or 50, or 4, 6, 8, 30, 50 for the list layout; any other value is stored as the smallest, with a warning. Omitted on POST, the smallest; omitted on PATCH, the stored limit stays unless a new layout's list lacks it. Not taken by link

position.description: first or last in the sidebar, last meaning before the bin widget when that is last; omitted with no after or before, a POST goes last

scope.description: space is the sidebar every member sees, written by the owner and admins; personal is this account's own sidebar in the space. Required on POST

target.description: id of the object the widget points at. Required on POST, refused on PATCH. Built-in listings cannot be added

view_id.description: which of the target's views a view widget shows. Only a query, collection or type target has views, and only a space widget keeps one

tools.name: update_widget
tools.description: Update a widget. Changes the layout, the limit or the view of a widget, or moves it with after, before or position. The path names the widget by its id or by its target; a target the sidebar holds in both scopes needs `scope`. The target itself does not change: delete the widget and create one for the other object.

after.description: id or target of the sidebar widget to move this one after. At most one of after, before and position; omitted, the widget keeps its position

before.description: id or target of the sidebar widget to move this one before

layout.description: link, tree, list, compact_list or view. The layout and the limit are re-validated as a pair whenever either is sent: a layout the target cannot render is replaced with the one it can, with a warning, and a stored layout the target cannot render is replaced the same way on a limit change

limit.description: how many entries a listing shows, from the app's own pick-list: 6, 10, 14, 30 or 50, or 4, 6, 8, 30, 50 for the list layout; any other value is stored as the smallest, with a warning. Omitted, the stored limit stays, re-fitted to the list of a new layout when that list does not hold it. With the link layout the stored limit stays untouched and a sent one is not stored

position.description: first or last in the sidebar, last meaning before the bin widget when that is last

scope.description: space or personal, when the target is in both

view_id.description: which of the target's views a view widget shows, by view id; an empty string returns to the target's first view. Only a query, collection or type target has views, and only a space widget keeps one

widget_id.description: Widget id, or the id of the object the widget points at

tools.name: delete_widget
tools.description: Delete a widget. Removes the widget from its sidebar. The object it pointed at is untouched. The path names the widget by its id or by its target; a target the sidebar holds in both scopes needs `scope`.

scope.description: space or personal, when the target is in both

widget_id.description: Widget id, or the id of the object the widget points at

tools.name: validate
tools.description: Validate an AnyBlock document. Structure and format rules only. Nothing is resolved against a space, so option names and a type's property keys are not checked here. Findings come back as data: an invalid document is still a 200, carrying the issues, and a valid one carries empty lists. Body: an AnyBlock document of any kind, checked without being stored; its schema and a worked example come from get_schema with kind document.
